long_biography.plain_text:
As a young Belgian Army lieutenant, Léon Hemeleers du Mortier had been made a knight of the Order of Leopold and awarded the Croix de Guerre. He married Una Shenley in London, and the compound Hemeleers-Shenley surname subsequently appeared in his military and public identity. The change marked a personal transition within an already decorated service career.

In the interwar years, Hemeleers-Shenley rose to commandant and lived at 4 Belgrave Square during an embassy posting. His work in Britain continued a career built around international military cooperation, now through formal representation rather than field-era liaison. He remained associated with the Belgian diplomatic mission in London and died in 1949.
